summary: Reviews the Initial Connection Protocol after RFC 165. An ICP committee had aimed for something that works quickly with few changes, and interviewed people with objections, ending in a compromise. The author notes the committee had no time to think about alternatives.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 197 proposes an alternative way for two hosts to establish a connection. It uses direct initiation and acceptance commands for one-way or two-way connections, with fewer setup exchanges.

questions: what is wrong with the icp in rfc 165
how was the icp committee formed
how did the alternative icp reduce setup steps
subtitle: A reviewed proposal for simpler simplex and duplex connection setup.

tldr.problem: The existing Initial Connection Protocol was adopted as a quick compromise, and its authors wanted to examine an alternative that required new Host-Host commands.
tldr.mechanism: The proposal defines commands to initiate, accept or refuse simplex and duplex connections directly through a listening server socket.
tldr.outcome: The authors argue this reduces setup exchanges and avoids the race condition described in earlier discussion.

today: RFC 197 is an ICP design review published in July 1971. The unit metadata lists its status as Unknown.

sections.title: Why Revisit the ICP
sections.content:
An ICP committee had been formed to produce a working solution quickly with minimal changes to the current protocol. After hearing objections, the group reached the compromise in RFC 165, but had little opportunity to consider alternatives.

This RFC proposes a simpler version of the ICP on the assumption that commands can be added to the Host-Host protocol. The authors hoped the proposal would inform a future protocol version.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier committee aimed for a quick compromise. This RFC sets out another design that could be considered when changing the Host-Host protocol.

sections.title: Connection Commands
sections.content:
For simplex connections, the user can issue ISC to initiate; the server can answer with ASC to accept or RSC to refuse. For duplex connections, IDC initiates, while ADC accepts and RDC refuses.

The acceptance command supplies the server-assigned socket information. After accepting, the server enters the connected state and sends the required ALL commands.
sections.plainLanguage: A user can request a one-way or two-way connection. The server can accept and provide connection details, or refuse the request.

sections.title: Expected Advantages and Alternatives
sections.content:
The proposal uses the server socket as an address for requests rather than connecting to that socket and exchanging additional setup information. The authors say this reduces the dialogue and avoids the race conditions described in RFC 143.

The RFC also suggests a smaller change to the current ICP: an accept command, or a CLS command with an added parameter to accept or refuse. The authors favor the larger modification.
sections.plainLanguage: The authors expect the new commands to reduce setup steps and avoid a known race. They also describe a smaller possible change, but prefer the larger redesign.
